newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish High Court extends Bell Lines protection.
newsitem.headline: Irish High Court extends Bell Lines protection.

text.p: Ireland's High Court on Wednesday extended protection to Bell Lines for two weeks after new investors came forward.

Bell examiner David Hughes has been engaged in intensive negotiations with new potential backers of a multi-million pound scheme in recent days to rescue the company and avoid a liquidation which would have drastic repercussions on the group's 200 employees, creditors and for the future of Waterford Port, media reports said.
An earlier plan to rescue the company, which has trading debts of around 20 million Irish pounds, collapsed last week, making liquidation likely.

A consortium of investors including Irish Continental Group, NatWest Venture Capital and Citycorp Venture Capital, which together own 85 percent of Bell Lines, pulled out of a proposed three million punt rescue package due to opposition from some leasing creditors.
Opposition came mainly from Waterford Harbour Commissioners and the Ministry for Marine which would have acted as guarantor of the port's debts.

Creditors opposed the scheme because they felt it unfairly prejudiced them over repayments for a 10 to 11 million Irish pounds loan to the European Investment Bank associated with the development of Waterford port.
Bell ran into difficulties in 1995 and 1996, mainly due to a freight price war on the North Sea and competition from the Channel Tunnel.
